title: San Diego holiday events, December 2026: parades, lights and where to stay
excerpt: The dates, times and costs for San Diego's biggest holiday events this December, from December Nights in Balboa Park to two boat parades on the bay, plus how to plan a stay around them.

seo.title: San Diego Holiday Events, December 2026: Dates and Tips
seo.description: San Diego holiday events for December 2026: December Nights, the Bay Parade of Lights, neighborhood parades, light shows and skating, with dates and costs.

heroCaption: Mission Beach and Mission Bay at dusk. The bay hosts its own boat parade of lights each December.
bodyHtml:
December in San Diego means boat parades instead of snow, a beachfront ice rink, and a free festival that fills Balboa Park for two nights. Below are the dates, times and costs for the season's main events as of November 2026, sorted by weekend, with notes on where to base yourself so you spend the evening at the event instead of in traffic.

As of November 2026

Every date below comes from the organizer or the San Diego Tourism Authority listing as published in early November 2026. Organizers do change times and routes, so check the linked page the week of your visit.

What are the biggest holiday events in San Diego in December 2026?

The anchor events are December Nights in Balboa Park (Friday and Saturday, December 4 and 5), the San Diego Bay Parade of Lights (Sundays, December 13 and 20), and neighborhood parades in Coronado, Ocean Beach and La Jolla on the first weekend of December. Around them run several weeks of light shows, a beachfront skating rink in Coronado, and holiday programming at the Zoo, SeaWorld and LEGOLAND.

When is December Nights in Balboa Park, and is it free?

December Nights runs Friday, December 4, from 4 p.m. to 10 p.m. and Saturday, December 5, from noon to 10 p.m. Admission is free. The City of San Diego describes it as its largest free holiday festival, with more than 350,000 visitors over the two days, so plan on crowds after dark.

Expect live music on several stages, food and craft vendors along El Prado, and the park's Spanish Colonial buildings lit for the season. The City's December Nights page lists the stage schedule and the getting-there options. Parking inside the park fills early on both days, so families with young children often go on Saturday afternoon, when the festival opens at noon and the crowds are lighter.

When and where can you watch the San Diego Bay Parade of Lights?

The Bay Parade of Lights sails on two Sundays, December 13 and December 20, starting at 5:30 p.m. from Shelter Island. Watching from shore is free. This year's theme is "Liberty Lights the Bay: Cheers to 250 Years," and it is the parade's 56th edition.

The boats pass Harbor Island, the Embarcadero, Seaport Village and The Port Park and Pier in Barrio Logan, then cross toward the Coronado Bridge and finish near the Coronado Ferry Landing. The Embarcadero and Seaport Village have the most room to stand; the Ferry Landing gives a view of the finish with the downtown skyline behind it. For a seat on the water, the Maritime Museum of San Diego sells parade-night tickets aboard its historic ships, starting at $55 for adults on the Star of India, and estimates the boats reach its waterfront around 6:20 p.m.

Is there a boat parade on Mission Bay too?

Yes. The Mission Bay Christmas Boat Parade of Lights is listed for Saturday, December 12, by the San Diego Tourism Authority, and it opens with fireworks from SeaWorld. The shoreline along Mission Bay Drive and the bayside walk in Mission Beach and Pacific Beach are the usual places to watch. A stay in Mission Beach puts the bay a short walk from the front door.

Which neighborhood holiday parades are worth planning around?

Three neighborhood parades fall on the first weekend of December. Each is free, and each is small enough to enjoy with children without a long walk from parking.

  • Coronado Holiday Parade, Friday, December 4. The parade runs from the Ferry Landing down Orange Avenue to the Hotel del Coronado, with a tree lighting at Rotary Park.
  • Ocean Beach Holiday Parade, Saturday, December 5, at 5 p.m. Floats, bands and local groups along Newport Avenue.
  • La Jolla Christmas Parade and Holiday Festival, Sunday, December 6, at 1 p.m. The parade moves through the Village from Girard Avenue, and a free festival runs from 1 to 5 p.m. at the La Jolla Recreation Center.

If you are staying a long weekend, these three can be paired with December Nights: Coronado on Friday evening, Balboa Park on Saturday afternoon and Ocean Beach that evening, and La Jolla on Sunday. Our La Jolla neighborhood guide covers where to eat once the parade ends.

Where are the best holiday light displays in San Diego?

The largest ticketed light shows this season are Lightscape at San Diego Botanic Garden in Encinitas, Coastal Christmas at the Del Mar Fairgrounds, and Jungle Bells at the San Diego Zoo. All three require tickets or admission, and the weekends before Christmas sell out first.

  • Lightscape, San Diego Botanic Garden, Encinitas. Nightly from 5 p.m., November 20, 2026, through January 3, 2027. Tickets start at $28 for adults and $18 for children; ages 2 and under are free.
  • Coastal Christmas, Del Mar Fairgrounds. Listed for December 11 to 26, 2026, with tickets sold in advance only.
  • Jungle Bells, San Diego Zoo. December 19, 2026, through January 3, 2027, with evening hours until 8 p.m. It is included with Zoo admission. The Zoo notes an exception on December 24, so check that date before you plan around it.

Can you ice skate on the beach in San Diego?

Yes. Skating by the Sea at the Hotel del Coronado sets up an ice rink on the resort's beachfront Windsor Lawn, open daily from November 20, 2026, through January 3, 2027. Sessions last 90 minutes, skate rental is included, and tickets run $35 to $45 depending on the date. Tickets are sold online or by phone, and the hotel recommends booking ahead.

The rink is one of the easier holiday outings with young children because it fits in a morning. A base in Coronado puts it, the Coronado parade and the Ferry Landing view of the Bay Parade of Lights within a short drive or bike ride.

What holiday events do SeaWorld, LEGOLAND and the Symphony run?

SeaWorld San Diego and LEGOLAND California both run holiday seasons that stretch from mid or late November into early January, and the San Diego Symphony plays three nights of holiday concerts at The Rady Shell on the bay. Check each park's ticket page for what your admission covers.

  • SeaWorld San Diego Christmas Celebration: November 13, 2026, through January 3, 2027, with nightly light shows and fireworks on select nights, including Saturday, December 12.
  • LEGOLAND California Holidays, Carlsbad: select dates from November 21 through January 3, including most of the week between Christmas and New Year's.
  • San Diego Symphony at The Rady Shell: holiday concerts December 18 to 20.

If you would rather spend the week outside the parks, our guide to family days beyond the big parks covers Balboa Park museums, tide pools and the Birch Aquarium, most of which run normal hours through the holidays.

Where should you stay for the holidays in San Diego?

Choose your base by the events you care about most. Downtown and Coronado put you closest to the Bay Parade of Lights and December Nights. Mission Beach and Pacific Beach suit the Mission Bay parade and SeaWorld. La Jolla, Del Mar and Encinitas sit nearest the La Jolla parade, Coastal Christmas and Lightscape.

A vacation rental also solves the logistics a hotel room does not: a kitchen for a holiday dinner, room for visiting family under one roof, and parking for the car you will want for the evening events. Cardo's homes across the coast, from Coronado to Encinitas, can be booked directly at booking.cardorentals.com. The week between Christmas and New Year's is one of the busiest of the winter, so it is worth reserving early.

Weekend at a glance

Dec 4 to 6: Coronado parade, December Nights, OB parade, La Jolla parade. Dec 12 and 13: Mission Bay boat parade with SeaWorld fireworks, then the first Bay Parade of Lights. Dec 18 to 20: Jungle Bells opens, symphony at The Rady Shell, second Bay Parade of Lights. All month: Lightscape, Skating by the Sea, Coastal Christmas from Dec 11.
